content.text: All six preferred elements appear across §§ 13.1–13.3, with § 24.1 supporting successor assignment. No redline needed.

input.quote: 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.
input.rationale: The licence package meets the preferred position in full. § 13.1 grants the subscription rights to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf (no written-notice condition needed); § 13.2 makes paid-up and Deliverable-embedded software perpetual and irrevocable for Customer and its Affiliates, with contractor support permitted; § 13.3 bars Vendor from revoking or suspending a licence except for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a cure opportunity, and permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by § 24 (which, at § 24.1, allows consent-free assignment to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or asset sale). § 14.3 confirms the § 13.2 perpetual licence reaches Vendor Technology needed to use a Deliverable. Noted only as context: § 14.2 gives Customer a "revocable, non-transferable licence" in Deliverables, which conflicts with this section; we address that Deliverable-ownership/licence term once under the IP rule rather than duplicating it here.
